northbank/csv-export-format: Northbank CLI refunds_csv (and any future CSV export) uses a hand-rolled minimal escaper in cli.py csv_field(), not the stdlib csv module. Contract: quote a field only if it contains a comma, double quote, CR, or LF; double embedded double quotes; LF line endings with one final LF; empty result is header "id,posted_at,amount_cents" plus LF. Rationale: csv.writer with lineterminator="\n" does not quote fields containing CR (stdlib quotes only delimiter/quotechar/chars-in-terminator), and its excel dialect emits CRLF, so both violate the contract. Rows come from provider.LedgerLake.list_transactions, which already returns posting-instant-then-ID order; posted_at strings are emitted verbatim (offsets preserved). Established in trial-74w.
northbank/incident-replay-freeze: northbank/cli incident_replay freeze: The incident_replay op (added for INC-204, issue trial-3z6) is a permanent frozen reproduction of the corrected release-1 statement. It computes its own month window inline (begin = month first calendar date 00:00 UTC inclusive, end = next month first calendar date 00:00 UTC exclusive, absolute-instant UTC comparison via the LedgerLake adapter). It must NOT be refactored to delegate to reconcile() or month_window(): reconcile is the active accounting report and may change behavior in later issues, while incident_replay must keep reproducing the corrected statement forever. It does not alter reconcile or refunds_csv. The transactions override applies as with every op.
northbank/ledger-day-bucketing: northbank/cli daily_net ledger-day bucketing (issue trial-1un, 2026-09-07): daily_net is an ACTIVE report: it takes its rows from month_window() exactly like reconcile (finance ledger month, see northbank/ledger-month-cutoff). Inside that window each posting belongs to the ledger day that began at 05:00:00 UTC on its calendar date: cli.py ledger_day() converts posted_at to a UTC instant, keeps the UTC calendar date when hour >= 5, and takes the previous date for instants 00:00:00.000-04:59:59.999. A timestamp written calendar date never determines the bucket (offset timestamps compare as absolute instants). Consequences: the window opening 05:00 UTC on the months first date maps to that first date, and postings from 00:00 to <05:00 UTC on the next months first date map to the requested months last calendar date (issue example: 2025-03-01T04:30:00Z is ledger day 2025-02-28). Output: only dates with at least one included transaction appear (zero-net days stay), ordered by date; empty month gives days: []. Bundled snapshot February 2025 daily_net: 2025-02-10 pay 12000 net 12000; 2025-02-27 pay 2500 (p-feb-last posted 2025-02-28T00:00:00Z falls pre-dawn onto the 27th); 2025-02-28 pay 9700 refund 400 net 9300 (p-mar-open + p-offset-feb + r-feb-last). The days sum exactly to reconcile: 24200/400/23800.
northbank/ledger-month-cutoff: northbank/cli ledger month cutoff (issue trial-c55, 2026-09-07): The finance ledger month is permanent for all ACTIVE reports. month_window() in cli.py returns [first calendar date of the month 05:00:00 UTC inclusive, first calendar date of next month 05:00:00 UTC exclusive]. The 05:00 cutoff is fixed year-round in UTC (no daylight-saving shift) and applies to every requested month including past years and December-to-January rollover. reconcile and refunds_csv both use month_window and therefore this definition. Absolute-instant UTC comparison of posted_at (including numeric-offset timestamps) is unchanged, done by the LedgerLake adapter. incident_replay is NOT on this definition: it stays frozen on the complete UTC calendar month 00:00-00:00 per its own inline window and the northbank/incident-replay-freeze memory. Bundled snapshot February 2025 ledger-month reconcile: ids p-feb-mid, p-feb-last, r-feb-last, p-offset-feb, p-mar-open; payments 24200, refunds 400, net 23800 (p-mar-open at 2025-03-01T00:00:00Z is inside February because the close is 2025-03-01T05:00:00Z).
